neighbours.label: The verb or modal that opens the second predicate of a coordination after 'and' (and can be, and could barely, and switch), vs the same sentences with a single predicate or a copula after 'and'
fire: The tiles are light and can be cut with an ordinary saw.
She practised all winter and could finally play the whole piece.
The bags fold flat and can be stored in a small drawer.
The old man walked slowly and could barely climb the stairs.
The tents are cheap and can be set up in five minutes.
He ran to the corner and could just see the bus pulling away.
These seeds grow quickly and can be harvested in a month.
The puppy was tired and could hardly keep its eyes open.
quiet: The tiles are light and easy to cut with an ordinary saw.
She practised all winter, so the whole piece was finally ready.
The bags fold flat and fit in a small drawer.
The old man walked slowly up the stairs.
The tents are cheap and quick to set up.
He ran to the corner just as the bus was pulling away.
These seeds grow quickly and are ready in a month.
The puppy was tired and very sleepy.

predictions: Fire items 0.15-0.35 on the modal or verb after 'and'; near misses under 0.08. A weak pole.
notes: Card: ' can' x5, ' could' x3, ' or' x3, ' switch', mostly right after 'and' joining a second verb phrase. Probe: 'and can be installed' 0.265, 'and could barely' 0.261, 'and switch to a taxi' 0.197; 'and are installed' 0.066, 'He can swim' 0.044, 'honey or syrup' 0.029.
